# Bhavitta

> Bhavitta is a free, private, on-device retirement-readiness check and planning app for iPhone (iOS 18+) and Android. You map your whole financial life as a timeline of life stages, and the app simulates it with 10,000 Monte Carlo trials or by replaying real market history from 1928 to 2025, then gives a 0 to 100 readiness score, a probability fan of outcomes, a stress-test heatmap and a year-by-year ledger. There is no account and no server: the plan never leaves the phone.

The name is Sanskrit: bhavishya (future) + vitta (wealth). Built and maintained by one independent developer, Balaji Gururajan, who also writes the guides. Not backed by a bank, brokerage, or advisory firm. Not financial advice.

This file is the full text of every guide on bhavitta.com, generated from the pages (SiteTools/site_seo.py). The short index is https://bhavitta.com/llms.txt.


---

# Is ₹3 crore enough to retire in India? Chance by spending and age

URL: https://bhavitta.com/is-3-crore-enough-to-retire-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-05

Short answer. It depends mostly on what you spend. For a couple spending ₹1 lakh a month, ₹3 crore lasts to 90 in only 46% of market paths if they stop work at 45, 53% at 50 and 62% at 55. On ₹75,000 a month it reaches 83% from 55, enough by the app's 80% bar. To spend ₹1 lakh a month with an 80% chance you need about ₹4.4 crore at 45, ₹4.05 crore at 50 and ₹3.7 crore at 55, in today's money.

"Is ₹3 crore enough?" is one of the most common questions on Indian FIRE and personal-finance forums, and the replies usually split between "easily" and "not even close". Both can be right, because the answer turns on two things the question leaves out: how much you spend each month and how many years the money has to last. The tables below come from Bhavitta's own engine, the same one the app runs: 10,000 simulated market paths for each figure, in rupees, for a couple who stop working at 40, 45, 50 or 55 and need the money to last to 90.

### What chance does ₹3 crore give you?

The share of 10,000 market paths in which ₹3 crore lasts to 90, by monthly spending and the age you stop working. Spending is in today's rupees and rises with inflation; health insurance is on top.

*Share of 10,000 simulated paths in which ₹3 crore lasted to 90. Couple, no income after stopping; spending in today's rupees rising with Bangalore inflation (5%); health insurance ₹40,000 a year rising 10% on top; Balanced India Monte Carlo (9.5% mean, 13% volatility), 10,000 trials; must last every year to 90. Bhavitta 2.9 engine.*

| Monthly spending | Stop at 40 | Stop at 45 | Stop at 50 | Stop at 55 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ₹75,000 | 66% | 72% | 78% | 83% |
| ₹1 lakh | 41% | 46% | 53% | 62% |
| ₹1.5 lakh | 10% | 12% | 15% | 20% |
| ₹2 lakh | 1% | 1% | 2% | 3% |

So ₹3 crore is enough for a couple spending up to about ₹75,000 a month from their mid-fifties. Stopping at 45 on ₹1 lakh a month is closer to a coin toss. Download this table (CSV).

Try this ₹3 crore scenario in Bhavitta. Set the currency to INR and build a plan for a couple aged 45 with ₹3 crore saved and no income, living in Bangalore. On My Plan, open the Bangalore stage and set yearly spending to ₹12 lakh (₹1 lakh a month). From "Add a life event", add Health insurance at ₹40,000 a year, rising 10%. The plan's chance should come out at about 46%; then drag the savings slider on Projections to find your own number. Free on App Store · Google Play.

### How much do you need for ₹1 lakh a month?

The smallest corpus, to the nearest ₹5 lakh, that lasts to 90 in at least 80% of paths:

| Monthly spending | Stop at 40 | Stop at 45 | Stop at 50 | Stop at 55 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ₹75,000 | ₹3.65 Cr | ₹3.40 Cr | ₹3.10 Cr | ₹2.85 Cr |
| ₹1 lakh | ₹4.70 Cr | ₹4.40 Cr | ₹4.05 Cr | ₹3.70 Cr |
| ₹1.5 lakh | ₹6.70 Cr | ₹6.40 Cr | ₹5.90 Cr | ₹5.40 Cr |
| ₹2 lakh | ₹8.80 Cr | ₹8.30 Cr | ₹7.75 Cr | ₹7.10 Cr |

A quick rule from this table: you need about 30 times your yearly spending if you stop at 55, 34 times at 50, 37 times at 45 and close to 40 times at 40. The "25 times expenses" rule, which is the US 4% rule in another form, falls short in every row.

### What about ₹2, ₹4, ₹5 or ₹6 crore?

For a couple stopping work at 45, the chance of the money lasting to 90:

| Monthly spending | ₹2 Cr | ₹3 Cr | ₹4 Cr | ₹5 Cr | ₹6 Cr |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| ₹75,000 | 31% | 72% | 88% | 95% | 98% |
| ₹1 lakh | 10% | 46% | 73% | 87% | 94% |
| ₹1.5 lakh | 0% | 12% | 36% | 60% | 75% |
| ₹2 lakh | 0% | 1% | 13% | 31% | 51% |

The jump from ₹2 crore to ₹3 crore matters more than any later step: on ₹75,000 a month it takes the chance from 31% to 72%. Past about 35 times spending, each extra crore buys less. For smaller and larger amounts, see Is ₹1 crore enough? and Is ₹5 crore enough?

### What the numbers assume

- A couple with no further income. The corpus is everything they hold the day they stop working: no salary, rent, pension or annuity after that.
- Monthly spending in today's rupees, rising with Bangalore's inflation of 5% a year (state CPI-Urban). Health insurance comes on top: ₹40,000 a year today, rising 10% a year.
- Returns from the app's Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility, all in rupees. 10,000 trials per figure.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero in every year to 90, not just at the end. 80% is the bar the app uses for "ready".
- EPF, PPF and NPS count inside the corpus. If part of it is locked until 58 or 60, the liquid part has to carry you until then.
- No tax in retirement. Add a tax rate to the retirement stage in the app if your withdrawals will be taxed.

### What changes the answer most

- Spending, by far. Going from ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh a month adds about ₹2 crore to what you need, more than retiring ten years later saves.
- Owning your home. Rent is usually the biggest monthly line. A paid-off home can take ₹25,000–50,000 off the monthly figure, which at 45 is worth roughly ₹1–2 crore of corpus.
- A bad first few years. The app's "A crash in your first year" line shows how much an early downturn costs. It is the main reason the multiples here are higher than the 4% rule.
- Any income at all. A pension, rent or a few years of part-time work shortens the stretch the corpus has to cover alone.
- Where you live. The city sets both the cost and the inflation rate; the corpus-by-city guide gives the number for seven Indian cities, and Mumbai vs Pune follows one couple through the choice.

### Common questions

#### Is ₹3 crore enough to retire at 45 in India?

For a couple spending ₹1 lakh a month, no: ₹3 crore lasts to 90 in 46% of 10,000 simulated market paths. On ₹75,000 a month it is 72%, just short of the 80% bar. To spend ₹1 lakh a month from 45 with an 80% chance you need about ₹4.4 crore.

#### Is ₹3 crore enough to retire at 55?

On ₹75,000 a month, yes: 83% of paths last to 90. On ₹1 lakh a month it is 62%, and you would need about ₹3.7 crore for an 80% chance.

#### How much monthly income can ₹3 crore give?

Roughly ₹75,000 a month in today's money, rising with inflation, for a couple from about 55 with an 80% chance of lasting to 90. Stopping earlier means less: ₹75,000 a month from 45 needs ₹3.4 crore.

#### Is ₹2 crore enough to retire in India?

Not for a couple spending ₹75,000 a month or more: ₹2 crore lasts to 90 in 31% of paths from 45 and 45% from 55. It can work with lower spending, a paid-off home, a pension, or a later start.

#### Is ₹5 crore enough to retire at 45?

For ₹1 lakh a month, yes: 87% of paths last to 90. For ₹1.5 lakh a month it is 60%; that lifestyle needs about ₹6.4 crore from 45.

#### How many times my annual expenses do I need to retire in India?

On these assumptions, about 30 times your yearly spending to stop at 55, 34 times at 50, 37 times at 45 and close to 40 times at 40, for an 80% chance of lasting to 90. That is a withdrawal rate of 2.5–3.3%, below the 4% often quoted.

### Run your own number

- Set the currency to INR at the top of the app. New plans start with Indian defaults: resident cost of living, city inflation and the Balanced India return preset.
- On the Start tab, enter your age, savings, income and city. To use your own monthly figure, open the city stage on My Plan and type your yearly spending.
- Add Health insurance, EPF, PPF, NPS and any pension from "Add a life event".
- The Projections tab shows your chance of lasting to 90, the earliest age you could stop at 80%, and a savings slider to try ₹3 crore against your own spending.

Educational, not advice. These figures are the engine's output for invented households using Bhavitta's defaults and its own cost-of-living estimates. They are not a forecast and not a recommendation to retire at any age or with any amount. Returns, inflation, scheme rules and tax change; talk to a SEBI-registered adviser about your own situation.

# Moving back to India from the US: how much do you need to retire?

URL: https://bhavitta.com/moving-back-to-india-from-us.html
Last updated: 2026-11-05

Short answer. For a couple moving to Bangalore at 50 and spending ₹2.5 lakh a month, about $975,000 (₹8.4 crore) gives an 80% chance the money lasts to 90 on cautious returns of 7% a year, and about $575,000 if US markets repeat their history. On ₹1.5 lakh a month it is $600,000 (or $350,000); on ₹4 lakh a month, $1.55 million (or $925,000). A falling rupee works in your favour while your savings stay in dollars.

"How much do I need to move back?" comes up constantly among NRIs in the US, and it is harder than the usual retirement question because two currencies are involved. Your savings earn in dollars, your life costs rupees, and the exchange rate moves between them every year. The tables below come from Bhavitta's own engine, the same one the app runs, for a couple who stop working and move to Bangalore with a dollar portfolio. Each figure is the smallest corpus, in $25,000 steps, that lasts to 90 in at least 80% of simulated market paths.

### How much do you need to move back at 45, 50 or 55?

With cautious returns: the app's default Monte Carlo setting for a dollar portfolio, 7% a year on average with 12% volatility, 10,000 trials. Spending is in today's rupees.

| Monthly spending | Move at 45 | Move at 50 | Move at 55 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ₹1.5 lakh | $650k | $600k | $575k |
| ₹2.5 lakh | $1.05M | $975k | $925k |
| ₹4 lakh | $1.65M | $1.55M | $1.45M |

With US market history: the app's Historical setting, which replays every stretch of US market returns since 1928.

| Monthly spending | Move at 45 | Move at 50 | Move at 55 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ₹1.5 lakh | $375k | $350k | $350k |
| ₹2.5 lakh | $625k | $575k | $575k |
| ₹4 lakh | $975k | $925k | $900k |

Try this scenario in Bhavitta. Keep the currency on USD and build a plan for a couple aged 50 with $1 million saved and no income, living in Bangalore; a dollar plan starts on the cautious defaults (7% returns, 12% volatility, the rupee falling 3% a year). Switch the display to INR, open the Bangalore stage on My Plan and set yearly spending to ₹30 lakh (₹2.5 lakh a month), then add Health insurance from "Add a life event". The chance should land near the 82% in the table below. Free on App Store · Google Play.

The gap between the two tables is the honest range. History has been generous to US stocks; a planner who wants a margin of safety uses the first table. In both, the corpus works out to a first-year withdrawal of about 3.5% on cautious returns and 6% on history.

### Why does a falling rupee help?

Your costs are in rupees. If the rupee loses 3% a year against the dollar, as it has on average for the last decade, then each year a dollar buys more rupees and Bangalore's 5% inflation feels like about 2% in dollar terms. The dollar corpus needed at 50 on ₹2.5 lakh a month, by how fast the rupee falls:

*Smallest dollar corpus, in $25,000 steps, that lasted to 90 in at least 80% of simulated paths, for a couple moving to Bangalore at 50 and spending ₹2.5 lakh a month in today's rupees. Rupee spending converted at the scenario's ₹86 to the dollar; Bangalore inflation 5%; India health insurance ₹40,000 a year rising 10%; cautious = Monte Carlo 7% mean, 12% volatility, 10,000 trials; history = every US market window since 1928. Bhavitta 2.9 engine.*

| Rupee falls each year | Cautious returns | US market history |
|---|---|---|
| 0% (rupee holds) | $1.65M | $825k |
| 2% | $1.15M | $650k |
| 3% (the app's default) | $975k | $575k |
| 4% | $850k | $525k |
| 5% | $750k | $500k |

This is the single biggest assumption in an NRI plan. If the rupee held steady for 40 years, the cautious figure would rise by two-thirds. The app lets you set the rate yourself in Inputs. Download this table (CSV).

### Keep it in dollars or convert to rupees?

The same couple at 50 on ₹2.5 lakh a month, with the money either left in a dollar portfolio or converted at the scenario's ₹86 on arrival and invested in rupees (the app's Balanced India preset: 9.5% a year, 13% volatility, no currency effect). Chance of lasting to 90:

| Savings | Dollars, cautious | Dollars, history | Converted to rupees |
|---|---|---|---|
| $1M (₹8.6 Cr) | 82% | 96% | 71% |
| $1.5M (₹12.9 Cr) | 97% | 100% | 93% |
| $2M (₹17.2 Cr) | 99% | 100% | 98% |

On these defaults the dollar portfolio wins because 7% returns against roughly 2% dollar-terms inflation leaves a wider margin than 9.5% against 5% in rupees. That conclusion rests entirely on the rupee continuing to fall about 3% a year; at 0% the two are much closer. Many people who move back hold some of each, and the app can model both as separate plans.

### What about US Social Security?

If you have enough US work credits, Social Security can be paid to you in India; check your own case with the Social Security Administration's payments-outside-the-US screening tool. The dollar corpus needed at 50 on ₹2.5 lakh a month, with a benefit starting at 67:

| Social Security from 67 | Cautious returns | US market history |
|---|---|---|
| None | $975k | $575k |
| $12,000 a year | $850k | $550k |
| $24,000 a year | $700k | $500k |

### What the numbers assume

- A couple with no further income after the move: no salary, rent, pension or annuity unless stated.
- Monthly spending in today's rupees at Bangalore's 5% inflation. Health insurance comes on top: ₹40,000 a year today, rising 10% a year in rupees.
- Rupee depreciation of 3% a year against the dollar, the app's default (on annual averages of the Federal Reserve's INR/USD rate, FRED series EXINUS, the rupee fell about 3.1% a year from 2015 to 2025 and 4.7% a year from 1990 to 2025).
- Exchange rate of ₹86 to the dollar: the app's fixed conversion rate, and the input behind every figure here. The market rate was about ₹95.5 in October 2026 (FRED series EXINUS). At that rate the same rupee spending costs about 10% fewer dollars, so the dollar corpus figures here err on the high side, and $1 million converted on arrival would be ₹9.55 crore rather than ₹8.6 crore.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero in every year to 90.
- No tax in either country, and no currency-conversion costs. Both matter for NRIs: Indian tax residency, the RNOR period after you return, US tax for citizens and green-card holders, and how India taxes foreign funds can all change what you keep.

### Common questions

#### How much money do I need to move back to India from the US?

For a couple retiring to Bangalore at 50 on ₹2.5 lakh a month, about $975,000 for an 80% chance of lasting to 90 on cautious 7% returns, or $575,000 if US markets repeat their history. On ₹1.5 lakh a month it is $600,000 (or $350,000).

#### Is $1 million enough to retire in India?

For a couple spending ₹2.5 lakh a month from 50, yes: $1 million kept in dollars lasts to 90 in 82% of paths on cautious returns and 96% on US market history. Converted to ₹8.6 crore and invested in rupees it is 71%. On ₹4 lakh a month you would need about $1.55 million.

#### Should I convert my US savings to rupees when I move back?

On the app's defaults, keeping the money in dollars gave the better chance (82% vs 71% on $1 million), because a rupee falling 3% a year makes Indian costs cheaper in dollar terms. If the rupee stopped falling the advantage would shrink. This is a modelled comparison, not a recommendation; tax and fund rules differ by person.

#### How does rupee depreciation affect an NRI retirement plan?

A faster-falling rupee lowers the dollar corpus you need, because your rupee costs take fewer dollars each year. For ₹2.5 lakh a month from 50, cautious returns need $1.65 million if the rupee holds steady, $975,000 at 3% a year and $750,000 at 5% a year.

#### Can I get US Social Security if I retire in India?

US Social Security is generally payable to US citizens living in India, and a benefit lowers what your savings must cover. In the model, $24,000 a year from 67 cuts the cautious corpus for ₹2.5 lakh a month from $975,000 to $700,000. Check your own eligibility with the Social Security Administration's payments-outside-the-US screening tool.

### Run your own number

- Keep the currency on USD for a dollar portfolio, or switch the display to INR to see it in rupees.
- On My Plan, add a Move to your Indian city at the age you plan to go back. Set your own yearly spending on the city stage if you know it.
- In Inputs, set the rupee depreciation rate you believe, and add Social Security and India Health insurance from "Add a life event".
- Copy the plan, change one thing (the year you move, the city, rupees instead of dollars) and tap Compare. The Bangalore at 50 vs staying in Seattle example walks through the whole decision.

Educational, not advice. These figures are the engine's output for invented households using Bhavitta's defaults and its own cost-of-living estimates. They are not a forecast and not a recommendation to retire at any age or with any amount. Returns, inflation, scheme rules and tax change; talk to a SEBI-registered adviser about your own situation.

# How much do you need to retire in India? Corpus by city at 45, 50 and 55

URL: https://bhavitta.com/retirement-corpus-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-04

Short answer. For a couple living a comfortable resident lifestyle, retiring at 55 takes about ₹2.5–4 crore in today's money for an 80% chance the money lasts to 90: from ₹2.45 crore in Chennai and ₹2.5 crore in Pune to ₹3.05 crore in Bangalore and ₹3.95 crore in Mumbai. Retiring at 45 takes ₹2.95–4.7 crore. That is 28 to 36 times the first year's spending, a withdrawal rate of 2.7–3.6%, well under the 4% rule.

"How much do I need to retire?" usually gets answered with "25 times your expenses", a rule worked out on US market returns and US inflation. In India both are different: prices rise about 5% a year, health premiums faster, and a retirement at 50 has to last 40 years. The tables below come from Bhavitta's own engine, the same one the app runs, for a couple in each of the seven Indian cities the app has resident cost estimates for. Each figure is the smallest corpus, to the nearest ₹5 lakh, that survives to 90 in at least 80% (or 90%) of 10,000 simulated market paths.

### How much corpus do you need to retire at 55, 50 or 45?

Corpus at the day you stop working, in today's rupees, for an 80% chance it lasts to 90. That 80% is the bar the app uses for "ready".

| City | Spending in year one | Retire at 55 | Retire at 50 | Retire at 45 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mumbai | ₹13.3L | ₹3.95 Cr | ₹4.35 Cr | ₹4.70 Cr |
| Bangalore | ₹10.1L | ₹3.05 Cr | ₹3.35 Cr | ₹3.60 Cr |
| Delhi | ₹9.4L | ₹2.70 Cr | ₹2.90 Cr | ₹3.15 Cr |
| Goa | ₹9.4L | ₹2.65 Cr | ₹2.90 Cr | ₹3.15 Cr |
| Hyderabad | ₹8.8L | ₹2.70 Cr | ₹2.95 Cr | ₹3.20 Cr |
| Pune | ₹8.1L | ₹2.50 Cr | ₹2.75 Cr | ₹2.95 Cr |
| Chennai | ₹8.1L | ₹2.45 Cr | ₹2.70 Cr | ₹2.95 Cr |

Spending in year one is the app's resident cost of living for a couple in that city plus a ₹40,000 health-insurance premium. Delhi and Goa need a little less than their spending suggests because their prices rise 4.5% a year, not 5%.

### What if you want a 90% chance?

The same households, held to a stricter bar: the money lasts to 90 in nine of every ten market paths.

| City | Retire at 55 | Retire at 50 | Retire at 45 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mumbai | ₹4.75 Cr | ₹5.25 Cr | ₹5.65 Cr |
| Bangalore | ₹3.60 Cr | ₹4.05 Cr | ₹4.35 Cr |
| Delhi | ₹3.15 Cr | ₹3.50 Cr | ₹3.80 Cr |
| Goa | ₹3.20 Cr | ₹3.50 Cr | ₹3.75 Cr |
| Hyderabad | ₹3.15 Cr | ₹3.55 Cr | ₹3.90 Cr |
| Pune | ₹2.95 Cr | ₹3.30 Cr | ₹3.60 Cr |
| Chennai | ₹2.95 Cr | ₹3.30 Cr | ₹3.60 Cr |

Going from 80% to 90% costs roughly another 20% of corpus everywhere. Which bar to use is a judgement about how much a bad decade would hurt and how easily you could cut spending or earn again.

### Is the 4% rule safe in India?

Not for an early retirement on these assumptions. Dividing the first year's spending by the corpus in the 80% table gives the withdrawal rate each plan can afford:

| Retire at | 80% chance | 90% chance | Corpus as a multiple of spending (80%) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 55 | 3.3–3.6% | 2.8–3.0% | 28–31× |
| 50 | 3.0–3.3% | 2.5–2.7% | 31–34× |
| 45 | 2.7–3.0% | 2.3–2.5% | 33–36× |

Three things push the Indian figure below 4%. The gap between returns and inflation is narrower: the app's Balanced India preset averages 9.5% a year against 5% inflation, with 13% volatility. Health insurance grows at 10% a year, so it is a small cost at 55 and a large one at 85. And the horizon is long: 35 years from 55, 45 years from 45. The often-quoted "25× expenses" is the 4% rule in another form; on these numbers it falls well short.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple, already retired. The corpus is what they hold the day earned income stops. No salary, rent income, pension or annuity after that.
- Resident cost of living from the app's estimates for a comfortable couple, including rent: ₹12.9 lakh a year in Mumbai, ₹9.7 lakh in Bangalore, ₹9 lakh in Delhi and Goa, ₹8.4 lakh in Hyderabad, ₹7.7 lakh in Pune and Chennai (today's money). Each city inflates at its own rate from state CPI-Urban data.
- Health insurance at ₹40,000 a year today, rising 10% a year.
- Returns from the app's Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility, all in rupees. 10,000 trials per figure, each a different sequence of yearly returns.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero in every year to 90, not just at the end.
- EPF, PPF and NPS are inside the corpus. The table treats all savings as one pool you can draw from. If part of it is still locked (see below), you need more outside it.
- No tax in retirement. Tax on capital gains and interest is not modelled here. Add a tax rate to the retirement stage in the app if your withdrawals will be taxed.

### What changes the answer most

- Where you live. Mumbai needs about 60% more than Pune or Chennai for the same life, more than the difference between retiring at 45 and at 55. The Mumbai vs Pune worked example follows one couple through that choice with EPF, PPF, NPS and an EPS pension.
- Owning your home. The resident estimates include rent. A paid-off home takes a large share out of yearly spending, and the corpus falls roughly in proportion.
- A pension. Even a fixed EPS pension of about ₹1 lakh a year from 58 reduces what the corpus has to cover, though it buys less every year.
- Money you cannot touch yet. EPF pays out at 58, PPF matures after 15 years and NPS mostly at 60. Retire at 50 and the years until then come from the liquid part of your savings alone.
- Dollar savings. An NRI retiring to India with a US portfolio faces rupee depreciation as well as returns; see how much you need to move back from the US and Bangalore at 50 vs Seattle.

If you know your monthly spending rather than your city, Is ₹3 crore enough? gives the chance for ₹75,000 to ₹2 lakh a month at each retirement age.

### Common questions

#### Is ₹2 crore enough to retire in India?

Not for a couple at these resident cost estimates. Even at 55, the smallest corpus that reaches an 80% chance is ₹2.45 crore (Chennai). ₹2 crore can work with lower spending than the estimates here, for example in a home you own, in a smaller city, or alongside a pension.

#### Is ₹3 crore enough to retire in India?

At 55, yes in Pune, Chennai, Goa, Delhi and Hyderabad, where ₹2.45–2.70 crore reaches an 80% chance. Not in Bangalore (₹3.05 crore) or Mumbai (₹3.95 crore). At 45, ₹3 crore is enough only in Pune and Chennai.

#### Is ₹5 crore enough to retire in India?

Yes, in every one of the seven cities at 45, 50 or 55 for an 80% chance; the highest figure is ₹4.70 crore for Mumbai at 45. For a 90% chance, Mumbai needs ₹5.25 crore at 50 and ₹5.65 crore at 45.

#### How much do you need to retire in Mumbai?

About ₹3.95 crore at 55, ₹4.35 crore at 50 and ₹4.70 crore at 45, in today's money, for a couple spending ₹13.3 lakh a year including health insurance, with an 80% chance the money lasts to 90.

#### Should EPF, PPF and NPS count toward the retirement corpus?

Yes, but not as cash on day one. These tables count them inside the corpus. If you retire before 58 or 60, your liquid savings alone have to carry you until EPF and NPS pay out. The app models each scheme as its own account with its own payout age, so it shows that dip.

#### What is a safe withdrawal rate in India?

On these assumptions, about 3.3–3.6% of the corpus in the first year for an 80% chance when retiring at 55, and 2.7–3.0% when retiring at 45. For a 90% chance it is 2.8–3.0% at 55 and 2.3–2.5% at 45. The amount then rises with inflation each year.

### Run your own number

- Set the currency to INR at the top of the app. New plans start with Indian defaults: resident cost of living, city inflation and the Balanced India return preset.
- On the Start tab, enter your age, savings, income and city.
- Add EPF, PPF, NPS, Health insurance and any pension from "Add a life event" on My Plan.
- The Projections tab shows your chance of lasting to 90 and the earliest age you could stop working at 80%.

Educational, not advice. These figures are the engine's output for invented households using Bhavitta's defaults and its own cost-of-living estimates. They are not a forecast and not a recommendation to retire at any age or with any amount. Returns, inflation, scheme rules and tax change; talk to a SEBI-registered adviser about your own situation.

# Health insurance in retirement in India: how much it adds to your corpus

URL: https://bhavitta.com/health-insurance-retirement-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-05

Short answer. For a couple retiring at 55 in Bangalore, a ₹40,000 health-insurance premium that rises 10% a year adds about ₹30 lakh to the corpus they need: ₹3.05 crore instead of ₹2.75 crore for an 80% chance of lasting to 90. If premiums rise 13% a year it adds ₹45 lakh; a ₹80,000 premium adds ₹55 lakh. Retiring at 45, the same three cost ₹35 lakh, ₹75 lakh and ₹70 lakh. By 85 the premium is about ₹7 lakh a year, 14% of the couple's spending, up from 4% at 55.

Health cover is the expense that grows fastest in an Indian retirement. Employer group cover ends when the job does, a family floater has to be bought and renewed at retirement-age prices, and premiums rise faster than general inflation because both medical costs and your age push them up. Most retirement calculators fold health into a single inflation rate. Bhavitta models it as its own yearly cost with its own growth rate, so the tables below show what it adds on its own. Every figure is from the app's engine: 10,000 simulated market paths, in rupees.

### How much does health insurance add to the corpus?

The smallest corpus, to the nearest ₹5 lakh, that lasts to 90 in at least 80% of paths for a Bangalore couple at the app's resident cost of living, by premium:

| Health insurance | Retire at 55 | Retire at 45 |
|---|---|---|
| None (for comparison) | ₹2.75 Cr | ₹3.25 Cr |
| ₹40,000 a year, rising 10% (the app's default) | ₹3.05 Cr (+₹30L) | ₹3.60 Cr (+₹35L) |
| ₹40,000 a year, rising 13% | ₹3.20 Cr (+₹45L) | ₹4.00 Cr (+₹75L) |
| ₹80,000 a year, rising 10% | ₹3.30 Cr (+₹55L) | ₹3.95 Cr (+₹70L) |

The growth rate matters as much as the starting premium. From 45, three extra points of premium growth cost more than doubling the premium, because they compound over 45 years instead of 35.

### What will the premium be at 65, 75 and 85?

A ₹40,000 premium at 55, rising 10% a year, set against Bangalore's 5% general inflation:

| Age | Premium that year | In today's money | In today's money, at 13% |
|---|---|---|---|
| 55 | ₹40,000 | ₹40,000 | ₹40,000 |
| 65 | ₹1.04 lakh | ₹64,000 | ₹83,000 |
| 75 | ₹2.69 lakh | ₹1.01 lakh | ₹1.74 lakh |
| 85 | ₹6.98 lakh | ₹1.61 lakh | ₹3.62 lakh |
| 90 | ₹11.2 lakh | ₹2.04 lakh | ₹5.23 lakh |

For the corpus guide's Bangalore couple, health insurance is 4% of yearly spending at 55, 8% at 70 and 14% at 85. A plan that looks comfortable at 60 can be squeezed at 80 by this one line.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple with no further income, retiring at 45 or 55 in Bangalore at the app's resident cost of living (₹9.7 lakh a year today, rising 5% a year).
- Health insurance as a separate yearly cost from the day they retire: ₹40,000 today by default, rising 10% a year. Industry surveys put Indian medical inflation at 10–13% a year.
- Returns from the app's Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility. 10,000 trials per figure.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero in every year to 90. 80% is the bar the app uses for "ready".
- No claims, co-pays or uncovered bills. The premium is the only health cost here. Out-of-pocket costs come on top, and a one-time bill can be added in the app as a life event.

### Common questions

#### How much does health insurance add to my retirement corpus in India?

For a couple retiring at 55 in Bangalore, a ₹40,000 premium rising 10% a year adds about ₹30 lakh to the corpus needed for an 80% chance of lasting to 90. Retiring at 45 it adds about ₹35 lakh. Faster-rising or larger premiums add ₹45–75 lakh.

#### How fast do health insurance premiums rise in India?

Industry surveys put Indian medical inflation at about 10–13% a year, and premiums also step up with age bands. The app uses 10% a year by default; you can change it on the health-insurance item in your plan.

#### What will my health insurance premium be at 80?

A ₹40,000 premium at 55 rising 10% a year is about ₹4.3 lakh a year at 80 in that year's money, or roughly ₹1.3 lakh in today's money after 5% general inflation. At 13% a year it would be about ₹2.5 lakh in today's money.

#### Does employer health insurance continue after retirement?

Group cover through an employer usually ends when employment ends, so a retiree needs individual or family cover bought at their age. Buying before retirement, while still healthy, avoids fresh waiting periods on existing conditions. Check your own policy's terms.

#### Should health insurance be part of the retirement corpus calculation?

Yes, as its own line. A premium rising 10% a year is four times its starting size in today's money by 85; folded into 5% general inflation it would stay flat. Modelled separately, it adds ₹30–75 lakh to the corpus in these examples.

### Run your own number

- Set the currency to INR and build your plan on the Start tab.
- On My Plan, tap "Add a life event" and choose Health insurance. Set your premium and how fast you expect it to rise.
- Copy the plan, change the growth rate to 13%, and tap Compare to see what faster medical inflation does to your chance.

They are not a forecast and not a recommendation to retire at any age or with any amount. Returns, inflation, scheme rules and tax change; talk to a SEBI-registered adviser about your own situation.

# Which Indian city lets you retire earliest? Same salary, seven cities

URL: https://bhavitta.com/earliest-retirement-city-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-05

Short answer. On the same salary and savings, a couple can stop working years earlier in Pune, Chennai, Delhi, Goa or Hyderabad than in Bangalore or Mumbai. At 35 with ₹50 lakh saved and ₹30 lakh a year before tax, the app's engine gives an earliest retirement age of 47 in Pune, 48 in Chennai, Delhi and Goa, 49 in Hyderabad, 51 in Bangalore and 57 in Mumbai, for an 80% chance the money lasts to 90.

Where you live changes two things at once: how much you spend and how much of your salary you can save. Those compound together over a working life, so a city that costs ₹5 lakh a year more can cost a decade of work. The tables below take one couple, put them in each of the seven Indian cities the app has resident cost estimates for, and ask the app's solver for the earliest age they could stop working with an 80% chance of the money lasting to 90.

### Which Indian city lets you retire earliest?

A couple at 35 who work and retire in the same city, at the app's resident cost of living, with health insurance from today:

| City | Living cost, year one | ₹20L salary, ₹25L saved | ₹30L salary, ₹50L saved | ₹50L salary, ₹1 Cr saved |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Pune | ₹7.7L | 55 | 47 | 42 |
| Chennai | ₹7.7L | 55 | 48 | 42 |
| Delhi | ₹9.0L | 57 | 48 | 42 |
| Goa | ₹9.0L | 57 | 48 | 42 |
| Hyderabad | ₹8.4L | 56 | 49 | 42 |
| Bangalore | ₹9.7L | 60 | 51 | 44 |
| Mumbai | ₹12.9L | Not before 65 | 57 | 47 |

Salaries are gross, taxed under the new regime (9.6%, 15.9% and 22.0% effective). A one-year difference between cities with similar costs is within the simulation's noise; the gaps of three years and more are not.

### Why does Mumbai cost so many years?

Mumbai's resident cost estimate is about ₹5 lakh a year above Pune's, mostly rent. On a ₹30 lakh salary that is nearly a third less saved every year, and a larger pot needed at the end: about ₹3.95 crore at 55 in Mumbai against ₹2.5 crore in Pune (see the corpus-by-city guide). The two effects together turn 47 into 57. Higher incomes narrow the gap, because rent becomes a smaller share of what you earn: on ₹50 lakh a year the difference is five years.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple at 35 who keep the same job, in the same city, until they stop. Salary rises with the city's inflation, and nothing extra is saved beyond what is left after tax and living costs.
- Resident cost of living from the app's estimates for a comfortable couple, including rent, at each city's own inflation rate (5%; Delhi and Goa 4.5%).
- Health insurance at ₹40,000 a year today, rising 10% a year.
- Returns from the Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility. 10,000 trials.
- EPF, PPF and NPS are not modelled separately here; all savings are one pool. No children, home purchase or other big expenses.

### Common questions

#### Which is the cheapest city in India to retire in?

Of the seven cities the app has resident cost estimates for, Pune and Chennai are the cheapest at about ₹7.7 lakh a year for a comfortable couple, including rent. Delhi and Goa cost more today but have lower inflation (4.5% against 5%), so over a long retirement they end up close to Hyderabad.

#### Can I retire earlier if I move from Bangalore to Pune?

On these assumptions, yes. A couple at 35 with ₹50 lakh saved and ₹30 lakh a year could stop at 51 in Bangalore and 47 in Pune. Moving only at retirement also helps; see retiring in a metro, then moving.

#### How much do you need to retire in Mumbai vs Bangalore?

About ₹3.95 crore in Mumbai and ₹3.05 crore in Bangalore for a couple retiring at 55, in today's money, for an 80% chance of lasting to 90. The full table is in the corpus-by-city guide.

#### At what age can I retire on a ₹30 lakh salary in India?

For a couple at 35 with ₹50 lakh already saved, between 47 (Pune) and 57 (Mumbai) on these assumptions, for an 80% chance the money lasts to 90. Your own age depends on how much you spend and save; the app finds it for your numbers.

### Run your own number

- Set the currency to INR and enter your age, savings, salary and city on the Start tab.
- The Projections tab shows the earliest age you could stop working at 80%.
- Copy the plan, change the city on My Plan, and tap Compare to see how many years a move is worth.

# Retire in Mumbai, then move to a cheaper city: how much a later move saves

URL: https://bhavitta.com/retire-metro-then-move-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-05

Short answer. Moving later still saves a lot. A Mumbai couple retiring at 55 needs about ₹3.95 crore to stay in Mumbai, but ₹3 crore if they move to Pune at 65, ₹3.2 crore if they move at 70 and ₹3.45 crore at 75, for an 80% chance the money lasts to 90. On a fixed ₹3 crore, moving at 65 lifts their chance from 55% to 80%.

Many people want to spend the active first decade of retirement where their friends, family and doctors are, and move somewhere quieter and cheaper later, often a hometown. The question is whether a late move is worth planning for, or whether only moving on day one makes a difference. Bhavitta models a retirement as a series of stages, each with its own city, so a move at 65 or 70 is just a second stage. Every figure below comes from the app's engine: 10,000 simulated market paths, in rupees.

### How much does a later move save?

The corpus at 55, to the nearest ₹5 lakh, for an 80% chance of lasting to 90, by when the couple moves:

| When they move | Mumbai → Pune | Bangalore → Chennai |
|---|---|---|
| Never | ₹3.95 Cr | ₹3.05 Cr |
| At 75 | ₹3.45 Cr | ₹2.90 Cr |
| At 70 | ₹3.20 Cr | ₹2.80 Cr |
| At 65 | ₹3.00 Cr | ₹2.65 Cr |
| At 60 | ₹2.75 Cr | ₹2.60 Cr |
| At 55, straight away | ₹2.50 Cr | ₹2.45 Cr |

Moving from Mumbai at 65 saves almost ₹1 crore, two-thirds of what moving on day one saves. The step is smaller from Bangalore because Bangalore and Chennai are closer in cost.

### What does ₹3 crore buy a Mumbai couple?

Chance the money lasts to 90 for a couple retiring at 55 in Mumbai with ₹3 crore, by when they move to Pune:

| When they move | Chance of lasting to 90 |
|---|---|
| Never | 55% |
| At 75 | 68% |
| At 70 | 73% |
| At 65 | 80% |
| At 60 | 86% |
| At 55 | 90% |

### Why a late move still matters

Spending later in retirement is larger than it looks today, because it has had decades of inflation. A Mumbai couple's ₹12.9 lakh a year at 55 is over ₹40 lakh a year in that year's money by 80. Cutting the bill for the last 25 years of a 35-year retirement removes the biggest numbers in the plan. Health insurance does not change with the move, so it becomes a larger share of what is left.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple retiring at 55 with no further income, at the app's resident cost of living for each city (₹12.9 lakh a year in Mumbai, ₹9.7 lakh in Bangalore, ₹7.7 lakh in Pune and Chennai, today's money), each at its own inflation rate.
- No moving costs and no sale or purchase of a home. If a move frees up a Mumbai flat, the proceeds would add to the corpus; the app can model that as a home sale.
- Health insurance at ₹40,000 a year today, rising 10% a year, before and after the move.
- Returns from the Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility. 10,000 trials.

### Common questions

#### Should I retire in Mumbai and move to my hometown later?

On these numbers, a later move is worth a lot. A Mumbai couple retiring at 55 on ₹3 crore has a 55% chance of lasting to 90 if they stay, and 80% if they move to a Pune-cost city at 65. Your own answer depends on your hometown's costs and what you would do with a Mumbai home.

#### How much do you save by moving from Mumbai to Pune in retirement?

Moving at retirement cuts the corpus needed at 55 from about ₹3.95 crore to ₹2.5 crore. Moving at 65 cuts it to ₹3 crore, and at 70 to ₹3.2 crore.

#### Can I model a move partway through retirement?

Yes. In Bhavitta each stage of life has its own city, so a retirement in Mumbai until 64 and in Pune from 65 is two stages. The app's "Move" life event adds the second one.

#### Does moving to a cheaper city reduce health insurance costs?

Not much. Premiums depend mostly on age, cover and insurer, not the city, so the premium becomes a bigger share of a smaller budget after the move. These examples keep it the same before and after.

### Run your own number

- Set the currency to INR and build your plan with your retirement city on the Start tab.
- On My Plan, tap "Add a life event", choose Move, pick the city and set the age.
- Copy the plan with and without the move and tap Compare. If you own a home in the first city, add its sale as an event in the year you move.

# What if the market crashes the year you retire? Sequence risk in India

URL: https://bhavitta.com/market-crash-first-year-retirement-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-07

Short answer. A market fall in the first years of retirement does far more damage than the same fall later. For a Bangalore couple retiring at 55 on ₹3.05 crore, a plan with an 81% chance of lasting to 90 drops to 37% if their portfolio falls 30% in the first year, 48% if it falls at 60, 61% at 70 and 72% at 80. To keep 80% with a 30% fall at 55 they would need about ₹4.55 crore instead of ₹3.05 crore, or to cut their living spending by about a third.

This is sequence-of-returns risk. Two retirees can earn the same average return over 35 years and end up in very different places, because the order matters once you are withdrawing. A fall at 55 hits the largest balance you will ever have, and every year's withdrawal after it comes out of a smaller pot that has less left to recover with. The same fall at 80 hits a pot that has already done most of its work. Every figure below is from the app's engine: 10,000 simulated market paths, in rupees, with the crash replacing one year's return and every other year left to chance.

### How much does a crash in the first year hurt?

The chance that ₹3.05 crore lasts to 90 for a Bangalore couple retiring at 55, by the age the fall happens:

| Fall happens at | 30% fall | 40% fall |
|---|---|---|
| No fall (for comparison) | 81% | 81% |
| 55, the first year | 37% | 21% |
| 57 | 41% | 26% |
| 60 | 48% | 33% |
| 65 | 55% | 44% |
| 70 | 61% | 54% |
| 80 | 72% | 70% |

Even a 20% fall in the first year takes the plan from 81% to 54%. A 40% fall at 80 costs about 11 points; the same fall at 55 costs 60.

### What gets the plan back to 80%?

- A bigger corpus. With a 30% fall at 55 built in, the corpus needed for 80% rises from ₹3.05 crore to about ₹4.55 crore. That is the price of being sure about the worst first year, and it is why the readiness score in the app can be judged "vs bad markets".
- Spending less after the fall. Cutting living costs by 10% only gets the plan to 49%. Getting back to 80% takes living costs of about 64% of the plan, roughly ₹6.2 lakh a year instead of ₹9.7 lakh, with health insurance unchanged. Flexible spending helps, but one 10% trim is not enough after a fall this size.
- A mix that falls less. A 30% fall is what a mostly-equity portfolio might see in a bad year; the Nifty 50 lost more than half its value in 2008. A debt-heavy portfolio would fall much less. The equity vs debt guide sizes the fall to each mix.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple retiring at 55 in Bangalore with no further income, at the app's resident cost of living (₹9.7 lakh a year today, rising 5% a year), with health insurance at ₹40,000 a year rising 10%.
- Returns from the app's Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility. 10,000 trials per figure.
- The fall replaces that one year's return in every trial: the whole portfolio loses 30% (or 40%, or 20%) that year, and the years after it are random as usual. The engine does not assume a rebound.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero every year to 90. 80% is the bar the app uses for "ready".

### Common questions

#### What is sequence of returns risk?

It is the risk that bad returns arrive early in retirement, while you are withdrawing from your largest balance. Two retirees with the same average return can have very different outcomes depending on the order. For a Bangalore couple at 55 on ₹3.05 crore, a 30% fall in year one cuts the chance of lasting to 90 from 81% to 37%; the same fall at 80 cuts it to 72%.

#### What if the market crashes the year I retire?

In this example, the plan goes from an 81% chance of lasting to 90 to 37%. Getting back to 80% would take about ₹1.5 crore more at the start, or living on roughly two-thirds of the planned budget. A smaller fall, or a more conservative mix that falls less, does less damage.

#### How much more corpus do I need to protect against a crash?

For this couple, about ₹4.55 crore instead of ₹3.05 crore keeps an 80% chance even with a 30% fall in the first year. Your own figure depends on your spending, city and mix; the app's market-crash what-if computes it for your plan.

#### Is a crash later in retirement less dangerous?

Yes. A 30% fall at 70 leaves this plan at 61%, and at 80 at 72%, against 37% at 55. By then fewer years of withdrawals depend on the balance that fell.

### Test your own plan

- Set the currency to INR and build your plan on the Start tab.
- On Projections, the Adjust card's "A crash in your first year" row shows how many points a 30% fall at your retirement age would cost.
- For a different size or age, tap Market crash under "Try a shock" and set the age and the drop. Tap Save as new scenario to keep it, then Compare it with the original on Scenarios.

They are not a forecast and not a recommendation to retire at any age or with any amount. Returns, inflation, scheme rules and tax change; talk to a SEBI-registered adviser about your own situation.

# Equity or debt after retirement in India: which makes the money last?

URL: https://bhavitta.com/equity-vs-debt-after-retirement-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-07

Short answer. More equity after retirement raises what you are likely to leave behind but lowers the chance the money lasts. For a Bangalore couple retiring at 55 on ₹3.05 crore, an all-Indian-equity portfolio lasts to 90 in 73% of the app's market paths, a balanced one in 81% and a conservative, debt-heavy one in 85%, on the app's return assumptions. For a 95% chance, equity needs ₹6.15 crore, balanced ₹4.20 crore and conservative ₹3.50 crore. The equity plan's middle outcome still ends with more than twice as much money.

The usual advice is to own less equity as you age. The usual counter-argument is that a 35-year retirement needs growth. Both are right about different things: equity raises the average and widens the spread, and once you are withdrawing every year, the bad end of the spread is what runs a plan out. The tables below run the same couple through Bhavitta's three Indian return presets, 10,000 simulated market paths each, in rupees. They compare the presets' assumptions, not specific funds, and they are not a recommendation of any mix.

### How long does the money last with equity, balanced or debt?

The chance of lasting to 90 on a fixed corpus, and the smallest corpus (to the nearest ₹5 lakh) that reaches 80% and 95%:

| Preset (average return / volatility) | Retire at 55 on ₹3.05 Cr | For 80% | For 95% |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indian equity (11% / 20%) | 73% | ₹3.55 Cr | ₹6.15 Cr |
| Balanced India (9.5% / 13%) | 81% | ₹3.05 Cr | ₹4.20 Cr |
| Conservative India (8% / 7%) | 85% | ₹2.95 Cr | ₹3.50 Cr |
| Preset | Retire at 45 on ₹4.5 Cr | For 80% | For 95% |
|---|---|---|---|
| Indian equity | 82% | ₹4.20 Cr | ₹7.80 Cr |
| Balanced India | 91% | ₹3.60 Cr | ₹5.10 Cr |
| Conservative India | 97% | ₹3.55 Cr | ₹4.30 Cr |

The gap grows with the bar. At 80% the three presets are within ₹60 lakh of each other at 55; at 95% all-equity needs ₹2.65 crore more than conservative. Being nearly sure is what volatility makes expensive.

### Why does the lower-return mix last longer?

Three reasons, all visible in the engine. Volatility drags down the return you actually compound: an 11% average with 20% swings grows a lump sum at roughly 9% a year, close to the balanced preset. Withdrawals lock in losses, because selling after a fall sells more units at a lower price. And the spread cuts both ways: the equity plan's typical path ends richer, but its worst paths run out sooner.

The flip side is a crash. Sized to each mix, a 2008-style first year (equity down 40%, balanced down 25%, conservative down 10%) leaves the equity plan at 32%, balanced at 46% and conservative at 58%. See what a crash in the first year does.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple retiring in Bangalore with no further income, at the app's resident cost of living (₹9.7 lakh a year today, rising 5% a year), with health insurance at ₹40,000 a year rising 10%.
- The app's three Indian presets, nominal and before tax: Indian equity 11% average with 20% volatility, Balanced India 9.5% / 13%, Conservative India 8% / 7%. Real returns after 5% inflation are about 6%, 4.5% and 3%. If your debt earns less than 8% after tax, the conservative row is optimistic.
- The mix stays fixed for the whole retirement; there is no glide path or rebalancing schedule in these figures.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero every year to 90. 10,000 trials per figure.

### Common questions

#### How much equity should a retiree hold in India?

There is no single answer, and this is not advice on your own mix. On the app's assumptions, a debt-heavy mix gives the best chance of the money lasting for a couple at 55 on ₹3.05 crore (85% against 73% all-equity), while more equity leaves more behind in the typical case. The trade-off shifts with how much you have, how long it must last and what your debt earns.

#### Is 100% equity safe after retirement?

It raises the typical outcome and the risk of running out together. For this couple, all-equity has a 73% chance of lasting to 90 against 85% for a conservative mix, and a 40% fall in the first year takes it to 32%.

#### Why does a lower-return portfolio last longer in retirement?

Because withdrawals turn volatility into permanent losses: after a fall you sell more units to fund the same spending, and they are gone when prices recover. A steadier portfolio with a slightly lower average can therefore outlast a more volatile one, especially when you want a high chance of success.

#### Can I change the return assumptions in Bhavitta?

Yes. Inputs has the three Indian presets, and you can set your own average return and volatility. Copy your plan for each mix and use Compare to see both side by side.

### Run your own comparison

- Set the currency to INR and build your plan on the Start tab.
- Open Inputs and pick a return preset, or set your own average and volatility.
- Copy the plan on Scenarios, give the copy a different preset, and tap Compare.

Educational, not advice. These figures are the engine's output for invented households using Bhavitta's defaults and its own cost-of-living estimates. They are not a forecast and not a recommendation to retire at any age or with any amount. Returns, inflation, scheme rules and tax change; talk to a SEBI-registered adviser about your own situation.

# College, weddings, cars: how one-time costs change your retirement corpus

URL: https://bhavitta.com/one-time-costs-retirement-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-07

Short answer. Big one-time costs add to the corpus almost rupee for rupee, and together they add up fast. For a Bangalore couple retiring at 55, a child's last four years of college (₹8 lakh a year) add about ₹30 lakh to the corpus they need, a wedding at 60 (₹20 lakh today) about ₹20 lakh, two cars about ₹25 lakh and a round of home repairs about ₹15 lakh. All four together lift the corpus from ₹3.05 crore to ₹3.95 crore; without the extra ₹90 lakh, the chance of lasting to 90 falls from 81% to 53%.

Most retirement calculators ask for monthly spending and stop there. Indian retirements often carry a few large, lumpy costs on top: the end of a child's education, a wedding, a car or two, a house that needs work. They are easy to leave out because they are not "spending", and each one looks affordable on its own. The tables below add them to a plan one at a time and then together, using the app's engine: 10,000 simulated market paths, in rupees.

### How much do one-time costs add to the corpus?

For a Bangalore couple retiring at 55, the chance that ₹3.05 crore lasts to 90 and the smallest corpus, to the nearest ₹5 lakh, that reaches 80%:

| Cost (today's price) | Chance on ₹3.05 Cr | Corpus for 80% |
|---|---|---|
| None (for comparison) | 81% | ₹3.05 Cr |
| College, ₹8 lakh a year from 55 to 58 | 72% | ₹3.35 Cr (+₹30L) |
| Wedding at 60, ₹20 lakh | 75% | ₹3.25 Cr (+₹20L) |
| A car at 60 and another at 70, ₹12 lakh each | 75% | ₹3.30 Cr (+₹25L) |
| Home repairs at 65, ₹15 lakh | 77% | ₹3.20 Cr (+₹15L) |
| All four | 53% | ₹3.95 Cr (+₹90L) |

The four costs add ₹90 lakh in today's money between them, and the extra corpus needed is about the same. Each costs a few points of survival on its own; together they cost 28.

### Enter the price in the year you pay it

A one-time cost in Bhavitta is entered as the amount you will pay in that year, not today's price. A ₹20 lakh wedding five years from now costs about ₹25.5 lakh then at 5% inflation; a ₹12 lakh car bought 15 years from now costs about ₹24.9 lakh. The figures above use those grown amounts: ₹25.5 lakh for the wedding, ₹15.3 lakh and ₹24.9 lakh for the cars and ₹24.4 lakh for the repairs. College is different: it is a yearly cost entered in today's money, and the app grows it with inflation itself.

The further away the cost, the more this matters. Entering today's ₹20 lakh for a wedding five years away moves this plan by about one point; for a car fifteen years away, today's price would be about half the real one.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple retiring at 55 in Bangalore with no further income, at the app's resident cost of living (₹9.7 lakh a year today, rising 5% a year), with health insurance at ₹40,000 a year rising 10%.
- The costs: college fees of ₹8 lakh a year in today's money for four years from 55; a wedding at 60, cars at 60 and 70 and home repairs at 65, each at today's price grown 5% a year to the year it is paid.
- Returns from the app's Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility. 10,000 trials per figure.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero every year to 90. 80% is the bar the app uses for "ready".

### Common questions

#### How do I plan for my child's wedding in my retirement corpus?

Add it as its own cost in the year you expect to pay, at that year's price. For a Bangalore couple retiring at 55, a wedding costing ₹20 lakh today and paid at 60 (about ₹25.5 lakh then) adds about ₹20 lakh to the corpus they need for an 80% chance of lasting to 90.

#### Should children's education be part of the retirement corpus?

If the fees fall after you stop working, yes. Four years of college at ₹8 lakh a year from the first year of retirement adds about ₹30 lakh to the corpus in this example, and costs 9 points of survival on ₹3.05 crore.

#### How much extra corpus do I need for big expenses in retirement?

Roughly their total in today's money. College, a wedding, two cars and home repairs come to about ₹90 lakh at today's prices in this example, and the corpus needed rises by ₹90 lakh, from ₹3.05 crore to ₹3.95 crore.

#### Does it matter when a one-time cost happens?

Less than you might expect for a single cost. A wedding at 56 and one at 70 each leave this plan at 75%: the later one costs more rupees but comes out of a pot that has had longer to grow. What matters more is the total, and remembering to include them at all.

### Add your own costs

- Set the currency to INR and build your plan on the Start tab.
- On My Plan, tap "Add a life event" and choose Wedding, Kids' college or Big purchase. Set the age and the amount you expect to pay that year.
- Copy the plan without the costs on Scenarios and tap Compare to see what they cost you.

Educational, not advice. These figures are the engine's output for invented households using Bhavitta's defaults and its own cost-of-living estimates. They are not a forecast and not a recommendation to retire at any age or with any amount. Returns, inflation, scheme rules and tax change; talk to a SEBI-registered adviser about your own situation.

# Is ₹1 crore enough to retire in India? What it pays each month, by age

URL: https://bhavitta.com/is-1-crore-enough-to-retire-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-09

Short answer. For most couples, not on its own. ₹1 crore supports about ₹25,000 a month from 60 with an 80% chance of lasting to 90, ₹21,000 from 55 and ₹15,000 from 45, in today's money, with health insurance paid on top. On ₹40,000 a month it lasts in 41% of market paths from 60. A fixed ₹15,000-a-month pension lifts that to 66% and raises the safe figure to about ₹34,000.

"Is ₹1 crore enough to retire?" was the classic Indian retirement number for a generation, and it still comes up constantly. It was a lot of money when the question was first asked. The tables below come from Bhavitta's own engine, the same one the app runs: 10,000 simulated market paths for each figure, in rupees, for a couple who stop working at 45, 50, 55 or 60 and need the money to last to 90.

### How much can you spend each month on ₹1 crore?

The largest monthly spending, to the nearest ₹1,000, at which ₹1 crore lasts to 90 in at least 80% (or 90%) of paths. Health insurance is paid on top of these figures.

*Largest monthly spending at which ₹1 crore lasted to 90 in at least 80% / 90% of 10,000 simulated paths. Couple, no income after stopping; spending in today's rupees rising with Bangalore inflation (5%); health insurance ₹40,000 a year rising 10% on top; Balanced India Monte Carlo (9.5% mean, 13% volatility), 10,000 trials; must last every year to 90. Bhavitta 2.9 engine.*

| Stop working at | 80% chance | 90% chance |
|---|---|---|
| 45 | ₹15,000 | ₹10,000 |
| 50 | ₹18,000 | ₹13,000 |
| 55 | ₹21,000 | ₹17,000 |
| 60 | ₹25,000 | ₹21,000 |

₹25,000 a month is ₹3 lakh a year, which works out to a 3% withdrawal rate. That is lower than the 4% often quoted, because the premium grows faster than prices. By 90 it is about ₹1.6 lakh a year in today's money, so the corpus pays for more than the monthly figure alone suggests. Download this table (CSV).

Try this ₹1 crore scenario in Bhavitta. Set the currency to INR and build a plan for a couple aged 60 with ₹1 crore saved and no income, living in Bangalore. On My Plan, open the Bangalore stage and set yearly spending to ₹4.8 lakh (₹40,000 a month), and add Health insurance (₹40,000 a year, rising 10%) from "Add a life event". The chance should come out at about 41%; add a Pension / Social Security stage of ₹1.8 lakh a year from 60 with "Fixed in rupees" switched on, and it rises to about 66%. Free on App Store · Google Play.

### What chance does ₹1 crore give you?

The share of 10,000 market paths in which ₹1 crore lasts to 90, by monthly spending and the age you stop working:

| Monthly spending | Stop at 45 | Stop at 50 | Stop at 55 | Stop at 60 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ₹30,000 | 40% | 48% | 57% | 70% |
| ₹40,000 | 19% | 23% | 31% | 41% |
| ₹50,000 | 7% | 9% | 13% | 20% |
| ₹60,000 | 2% | 3% | 5% | 7% |
| ₹75,000 | 0% | 0% | 0% | 1% |

Even the frugal row falls short. On ₹30,000 a month, ₹1 crore reaches 70% from 60, still under the app's 80% bar, and from 45 it is worse than a coin toss.

### How much does a pension help?

A couple stopping at 60 with ₹1 crore, with and without a fixed ₹15,000-a-month pension from 60. The pension is in fixed rupees, like EPS or many employer pensions, so it buys less every year.

| Monthly spending | ₹1 crore alone | With ₹15,000 pension |
|---|---|---|
| ₹40,000 | 41% | 66% |
| ₹50,000 | 20% | 39% |
| ₹60,000 | 7% | 19% |
| ₹75,000 | 1% | 4% |

With the pension, the largest monthly spend at 80% rises from ₹25,000 to ₹34,000. A ₹15,000 pension adds only ₹9,000 to what you can spend, because it doesn't rise with prices: by 75 it buys about half what it did at 60.

### Is ₹1 crore enough in any Indian city?

Instead of a monthly figure, these use the app's resident cost of living for a comfortable couple in each city, including rent, and that city's inflation:

| City | Couple's cost a month | Stop at 55 | Stop at 60 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mumbai | ₹1,07,500 | 0% | 0% |
| Bangalore | ₹80,600 | 0% | 0% |
| Delhi | ₹75,300 | 1% | 1% |
| Goa | ₹75,300 | 1% | 2% |
| Hyderabad | ₹69,900 | 1% | 2% |
| Pune | ₹64,500 | 3% | 4% |
| Chennai | ₹64,500 | 3% | 4% |

A typical big-city lifestyle with rent costs two to four times what ₹1 crore can carry. The couples for whom ₹1 crore can work spend far less than these estimates: usually a paid-off home, a smaller town, and a pension or rent coming in.

### How much do you need for ₹30,000–₹50,000 a month?

The smallest corpus, to the nearest ₹5 lakh, that lasts to 90 in at least 80% of paths:

| Monthly spending | Stop at 55 | Stop at 60 |
|---|---|---|
| ₹30,000 | ₹1.30 Cr | ₹1.15 Cr |
| ₹40,000 | ₹1.65 Cr | ₹1.45 Cr |
| ₹50,000 | ₹2.00 Cr | ₹1.75 Cr |

For ₹75,000 a month and up, Is ₹3 crore enough? has the same table for stopping at 40 to 55.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple with no further income (except in the pension table). The corpus is everything they hold the day they stop working.
- Monthly spending in today's rupees, rising with Bangalore's inflation of 5% a year (state CPI-Urban). Health insurance comes on top: ₹40,000 a year today, rising 10% a year.
- Returns from the app's Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility, all in rupees. 10,000 trials per figure.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero in every year to 90, not just at the end. 80% is the bar the app uses for "ready".
- EPF, PPF and NPS count inside the corpus. If part of it is locked until 58 or 60, the liquid part has to carry you until then.
- No tax in retirement. Add a tax rate to the retirement stage in the app if your withdrawals will be taxed.
- City tables use the app's resident cost of living for a comfortable couple, including rent, and each city's own inflation rate, instead of a monthly figure.

### What changes the answer most

- Owning your home. At this budget rent can take a large share of the spending. Without it, ₹25,000 a month covers far more.
- A pension or rent. Any income that arrives every month shortens the stretch the corpus has to cover alone. One that rises with prices is worth much more than a fixed one.
- Health cover. The premium rising 10% a year is a large share of a ₹1 crore budget. Employer or government cover that continues after you stop work changes the picture.
- Working a few more years. Each year adds to the corpus and takes a year off the stretch it has to last; stopping at 60 instead of 55 adds about ₹4,000 a month.
- Where you live. The corpus-by-city guide gives the number each city needs, and retiring in a metro, then moving shows what a later move saves.

### Common questions

#### Is ₹1 crore enough to retire in India?

For most couples, no. ₹1 crore supports about ₹25,000 a month from 60 with an 80% chance of lasting to 90, plus health insurance, and less if you stop earlier. A typical big-city cost of living for a couple, ₹64,500 to ₹1,07,500 a month including rent, needs two to four times as much.

#### How much monthly income can ₹1 crore give?

About ₹25,000 a month in today's money, rising with inflation, for a couple from 60; ₹21,000 from 55, ₹18,000 from 50 and ₹15,000 from 45. Those keep an 80% chance of the money lasting to 90, with health insurance paid on top.

#### Is ₹1 crore enough to retire at 60?

Only on very modest spending. On ₹30,000 a month it lasts to 90 in 70% of paths, on ₹40,000 in 41%. With a fixed ₹15,000 monthly pension, ₹40,000 a month reaches 66% and the safe level rises to about ₹34,000.

#### Is ₹1 crore enough to retire at 45?

No, unless you spend very little: it supports about ₹15,000 a month from 45 at an 80% chance. On ₹30,000 a month it lasts in 40% of paths, on ₹50,000 in 7%.

#### How much do I need to retire on ₹50,000 a month?

About ₹2 crore if you stop at 55 and ₹1.75 crore at 60, for an 80% chance of lasting to 90, with health insurance on top. ₹40,000 a month needs ₹1.65 crore and ₹1.45 crore.

#### Is ₹1 crore enough for a single person?

These figures are for a couple's monthly spending, but the engine only sees the spending, so a single person spending the same amount gets the same answer. On ₹25,000 a month from 60, ₹1 crore has an 80% chance; enter your own figure in the app to check yours.

### Run your own number

- Set the currency to INR at the top of the app. New plans start with Indian defaults: resident cost of living, city inflation and the Balanced India return preset.
- On the Start tab, enter your age, savings, income and city. To use your own monthly figure, open the city stage on My Plan and type your yearly spending.
- Add Health insurance, EPF, PPF, NPS and any pension from "Add a life event".
- The Projections tab shows your chance of lasting to 90, the earliest age you could stop at 80%, and a savings slider to try your own corpus against your own spending.

# Is ₹5 crore enough to retire in India? Early retirement by age and spending

URL: https://bhavitta.com/is-5-crore-enough-to-retire-india.html
Last updated: 2026-11-09

Short answer. For a couple stopping work at 45, ₹5 crore supports about ₹1.17 lakh a month with an 80% chance of lasting to 90, ₹1.08 lakh from 40 and ₹1.01 lakh from 35, in today's money, with health insurance paid on top. On ₹1 lakh a month from 45 it lasts in 87% of market paths; on ₹1.5 lakh a month only 60%. At each city's typical cost of living for a couple, it clears 80% from 45 everywhere, and from 35 everywhere except Mumbai (76%).

₹5 crore is the number that comes up when people talk about retiring early in India, at 35, 40 or 45, rather than at 60. It sounds like more than enough, and for many lifestyles it is. But retiring at 40 means the money has to last 50 years, and the monthly figure it can carry is smaller than people expect. The tables below come from Bhavitta's own engine, the same one the app runs: 10,000 simulated market paths for each figure, in rupees, for a couple who need the money to last to 90.

### How much can you spend each month on ₹5 crore?

The largest monthly spending, to the nearest ₹1,000, at which ₹5 crore lasts to 90 in at least 80% (or 90%) of paths. Health insurance is paid on top.

*Largest monthly spending at which ₹5 crore lasted to 90 in at least 80% / 90% of 10,000 simulated paths. Couple, no income after stopping; spending in today's rupees rising with Bangalore inflation (5%); health insurance ₹40,000 a year rising 10% on top; Balanced India Monte Carlo (9.5% mean, 13% volatility), 10,000 trials; must last every year to 90. Bhavitta 2.9 engine.*

| Stop working at | 80% chance | 90% chance |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | ₹1,01,000 | ₹80,000 |
| 40 | ₹1,08,000 | ₹87,000 |
| 45 | ₹1,17,000 | ₹93,000 |
| 50 | ₹1,26,000 | ₹1,03,000 |
| 55 | ₹1,39,000 | ₹1,14,000 |

Stopping at 35 instead of 55 costs about ₹38,000 a month of spending for life. From 35, ₹5 crore is 41 times a year's spending at the 80% level, a withdrawal rate of 2.4%. Download this table (CSV).

Try this ₹5 crore scenario in Bhavitta. Set the currency to INR and build a plan for a couple aged 45 with ₹5 crore saved and no income, living in Bangalore. The chance should come out at about 87%; change the spending to ₹18 lakh a year and it falls to about 60%. Free on App Store · Google Play.

### What chance does ₹5 crore give you?

The share of 10,000 market paths in which ₹5 crore lasts to 90, by monthly spending and the age you stop working:

| Monthly spending | Stop at 35 | Stop at 40 | Stop at 45 | Stop at 50 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ₹1 lakh | 80% | 84% | 87% | 91% |
| ₹1.5 lakh | 51% | 55% | 60% | 66% |
| ₹2 lakh | 24% | 27% | 31% | 37% |
| ₹2.5 lakh | 9% | 12% | 13% | 17% |
| ₹3 lakh | 3% | 4% | 4% | 5% |
| ₹4 lakh | 0% | 0% | 0% | 0% |

The line falls between ₹1 lakh and ₹1.5 lakh a month. Up to ₹1 lakh, ₹5 crore works from any of these ages; at ₹1.5 lakh it stays below the bar even from 50 (66%). Spending matters far more than the age you stop: going from ₹1 lakh to ₹1.5 lakh costs more than stopping fifteen years earlier.

### Which cities does ₹5 crore work in?

Instead of a monthly figure, these use the app's resident cost of living for a comfortable couple in each city, including rent, and that city's inflation:

| City | Couple's cost a month | Stop at 35 | Stop at 40 | Stop at 45 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mumbai | ₹1,07,500 | 76% | 80% | 84% |

| Delhi | ₹75,300 | 93% | 95% | 96% |

| Hyderabad | ₹69,900 | 93% | 95% | 96% |

| Chennai | ₹64,500 | 95% | 96% | 97% |

At a typical comfortable lifestyle, ₹5 crore is enough to stop at 40 in every city, with Mumbai right at the bar. In Pune or Chennai it leaves a wide margin: room for travel, a car every decade, or helping children, which these figures don't include.

### Retiring at 35 or 40 on ₹5 crore

- Fifty years is a long time. From 35, the money has to outlast five decades of inflation, at least one or two deep market falls, and health costs that keep rising. That is why the safe withdrawal rate here is 2.4%, not 4%.
- The order of returns matters most early on. A bad first few years does more damage than the same fall at 70, because you are selling to live while prices are down.
- Some income helps a lot. Consulting, a small business or rent for even five years after stopping takes a large bite out of the risk. Add it as a stage in the app to see how much.
- Mix matters too. Equity or debt after retirement compares the app's three Indian return presets.

### What the numbers assume

- A couple with no further income, pension or rent. The corpus is everything they hold the day they stop working.
- Monthly spending in today's rupees, rising with Bangalore's inflation of 5% a year (state CPI-Urban). Health insurance comes on top: ₹40,000 a year today, rising 10% a year.
- Returns from the app's Balanced India Monte Carlo preset: 9.5% a year on average, 13% volatility, all in rupees. 10,000 trials per figure.
- Survival means the balance stays above zero in every year to 90, not just at the end. 80% is the bar the app uses for "ready".
- EPF, PPF and NPS count inside the corpus. If part of it is locked until 58 or 60, the liquid part has to carry you until then.
- No tax in retirement. Add a tax rate to the retirement stage in the app if your withdrawals will be taxed.
- City tables use the app's resident cost of living for a comfortable couple, including rent, and each city's own inflation rate, instead of a monthly figure.

### Common questions

#### Is ₹5 crore enough to retire in India?

For a couple spending up to about ₹1.2 lakh a month, yes, from 45: it supports ₹1.17 lakh a month at an 80% chance of lasting to 90, with health insurance on top. On ₹1.5 lakh a month it lasts in only 60% of paths from 45.

#### Is ₹5 crore enough to retire at 40?

On ₹1 lakh a month, yes: 84% of paths last to 90, and the safe level is about ₹1.08 lakh a month. At a typical comfortable cost of living it clears 80% in every one of the seven cities, with Mumbai exactly at 80%.

#### Is ₹5 crore enough to retire at 35?

Just, at ₹1 lakh a month: exactly 80% of paths last to 90. The money has to last 55 years, so anything above about ₹1 lakh a month falls below the bar.

#### How much monthly income can ₹5 crore give?

About ₹1.17 lakh a month in today's money, rising with inflation, for a couple from 45 at an 80% chance; ₹1.01 lakh from 35, ₹1.26 lakh from 50 and ₹1.39 lakh from 55.

#### Is ₹5 crore enough to live in Mumbai after retirement?

At the app's comfortable Mumbai cost for a couple, about ₹1.07 lakh a month including rent, ₹5 crore lasts to 90 in 84% of paths from 45, 80% from 40 and 76% from 35.

#### Is ₹5 crore enough for ₹2 lakh a month?

No: ₹2 lakh a month on ₹5 crore lasts to 90 in 31% of paths from 45 and 37% from 50. That lifestyle needs about ₹8.3 crore from 45 (see Is ₹3 crore enough? for the corpus table).
